phase3_findings.description: The DatabaseConfig.url validator accepts only mysql, mysql+<driver> or sqlite schemes, but build_sql_runner (factory.py:250), probe_database (preflight.py:115) and sqlglot_dialect_for_url (readonly.py:187) still accept any scheme starting with mysql, so an unvalidated Config or a direct call with mysqlx:// reaches MySQLRunner or pymysql instead of the unsupported-scheme refusal.

Same scheme mismatch as an error-handling risk: a programmatic caller that skips config validation with mysqlx:// fails later with a driver error rather than the structured unsupported-scheme error; no CLI path reaches it.

The four _BYPASS_CORPUS entries that put a MERGE inside a CTE (base lines 216-231, dialect postgres) were deleted, not moved to mysql; only the root-level MERGE at line 55 remains, which the root-type check refuses first, so the exp.Merge entry in the nested-write walk (readonly.py:377) has no test.

In test_call_after_nested_comment_markers_is_checked the row moved to ('mysql', 'sleep(0)', 'Nested MySQL comments') is refused by the nested-comment check before any function is examined, so it does not test what the test name claims.

The added comment 'sqlite_ is a catalog prefix only on sqlite.' is too broad: with no dialect or an unknown dialect every prefix counts, as the comment at line 162 says. Capped at Suggestion by the behavior-inert prose cap.

Untouched docstrings still name MariaDB's max_statement_time (line 30) and list 'aborted transaction' (lines 6-7), a PostgreSQL cause the diff removed from cleanup-error-handling.md. Capped at Suggestion by the behavior-inert prose cap.
